o: Sum all integers in [1, n] divisible by 3, 5, or 7. A simple loop over n ≤ 1000 works instantly, but the classic technique is inclusion–exclusion with the arithmetic-series formula: sum of multiples of d up to n is d·m(m+1)/2 where m = floor(n/d). Add singles, subtract pairwise intersections (15, 21, 35), re-add the triple (105).
k: Sum of multiples of d in [1,n] = d · m(m+1)/2 with m = ⌊n/d⌋.

a.i: Apply the closed-form per divisor and combine with signs per the principle of inclusion–exclusion; O(1) regardless of n.
Iterate 1..n and add numbers divisible by 3, 5, or 7 — dead simple and obviously correct; ideal for n up to 1e3 (or even 1e7).
s: For i in 1..n: if i % 3 == 0 or i % 5 == 0 or i % 7 == 0: ans += i.
a.t: O(n) — single pass over the range.

w: Mention both: the loop for clarity, inclusion–exclusion to show the scalable technique (essential if n were 1e12). Pitfalls: forgetting the +S(105) triple-intersection term, and integer division ordering in the formula. Follow-up: generalize to an arbitrary set of divisors (subset enumeration over 2^k masks).
